All ran exceptionally well but I think a special mention must be made of Gerry Leroy on the third stage in the final when he caught the Achilles man, bided his time, and then passed him to hand over a winning lead to Brian Morris.
Gerry Leroy ran very well in the half-mile to take 3rd place - he must have done his best ever. The race was won by Linford (T.V.H.) for Lensbury in 2m.0.8s., on a five laps to the mile grass track.

Gerry Leroy was bullied into running the 880 yds. and finished very fast to be placed second in 2m.0.6s. In the final of the 100 yds., Charlie, for some unknown reason was left at the start, but Dennis didn't wait for him and finished fifth in about 10.6.

Brian Morris, in serious preparation for a coveted place at Cardiff and Stockholm, sharpened his speed by running in both the 100 and 220 yds. events; comfortably winning the latter by a yard from Gerry Leroy in 23.2s.

Gerry Leroy and Henry Martin finished first and second in the 440 yds with 51.7 and 52.0s. respectively, although Gerry was rather disappointed with his performance, being hampered in training by a recurrent leg injury.

Pepe, running with great judgement in the outside lane, handed over with a two yard lead, after which our team were never headed and no doubt they would have beaten the existing best performance of 3m.28s. had Gerry Leroy not "coasted" during the middle part of the last lap.

This was not the only set-back, for we were minus all sprinters;they doing their best to record 2nd place behind the Valley, in the Southern 4 x 110 yards relay. It was therefore left to Gerry LeRoy to open our scoring. This he did with a vengance winning the quarter in a scintillating 49.4 secs.
But Gerry LeRoy had other ideas! Running like a man inspired he had caught Brian Morris, running for the Police, by the 220 and was hareing after the Valley.
Gerry LeRoy won a sparkling 440 running in the out-side lane, and the ever versatile Jimmy Heathfield returned to the distance over which he was winning 12 years ago, to win the quarter in 54.6 secs.

Both Gerry LeRoy and Charlie Jones qualified for the final of the quarter, despite Charlie feeling unwell owing to an attack of hay-fever. In the final, Gerry was drawn on the outside and Charlie in lane three;with Futter of University of London A.C., an AAA finalist the week previous.
Out to prove himself our best quarter miler Gerry LeRoy streaked past the line to win with a time of 49.0 secs, with Alan Jackson 3rd, in a personal best 50.6 secs.
Outstanding performance of the day was undoubtedly the quarter victory of tenacious Gerry LeRoy over his international opponent Chris Lindsey, both recording 48.7 secs.
Undoubtedly the best performance of the day was that of the victorious 4 x 440 yds team of Bernard Linley (still a junior!), Charlie Jones, Peter Eldridge and London Champion Gerry LeRoy.

Cruising home to a 49.8secs quarter win, Gerry LeRoy maintained his record of the last eight weeks - always passing the post first. Making a valuable contribution to our points, D.McCorquindale scored a double in the shot and discus, with 47 and 120 ft respectively.
Under the fierce glare of the floodlights Gerry LeRoy stepped on to the track and settled himself into his 'blocks'. With the 'Gun' and he was away very fast, in the outside lane.

Gerry LeRoy opened with a win in the "A" 100 in 10secs and later added the 440, when he convincingly defeated Brian Morris (running for his second claim club) in 49.3.

In a long-lasting battle for supremacy as Belgrave's best sprint man, Gerry LeRoy hoisted his penant high with a triple victory over close rival Peter Eldridge.
